state_machine.description: Initial and stopped state. All RunComd outputs are FALSE after stop/reset.

transitions.action: Clear all pumpGroup[i].RunComd to FALSE; stop wins over start.
Retain all RunComd FALSE; mode/priority/selection changes alone do not reselect.
Latch RunComd[i] := TopThree[i] computed from sampled priorities.

state_machine.description: Last start event was a manual selection. RunComd values are retained while neither start nor stop is TRUE.

transitions.action: Clear all pumpGroup[i].RunComd to FALSE; stop wins over start.
Retain all RunComd values; mode/priority/selection changes alone do not reselect.
Reselect and latch RunComd[i] := sampled pumpGroup[i].selection.
Reselect and latch RunComd[i] := TopThree[i] computed from sampled priorities.

state_machine.description: Last start event was automatic top-three selection. RunComd values are retained while neither start nor stop is TRUE.

transitions.action: Clear all pumpGroup[i].RunComd to FALSE; stop wins over start.
Retain all RunComd values; mode/priority/selection changes alone do not reselect.
Reselect and latch RunComd[i] := sampled pumpGroup[i].selection.
Reselect and latch RunComd[i] := TopThree[i] computed from sampled priorities.

timer_plan.reset_conditions: No PT timers are required. Stop/reset clears commands immediately. Each TRUE start scan re-latches the active command set immediately.
timer_plan.implementation_note: Stage 3 exists but contains no timer FB calls.

safety: 1. stop has absolute priority: if stop is TRUE, all five RunComd outputs are forced FALSE even when start is also TRUE.
2. Never write pumpGroup[i].priority or pumpGroup[i].selection; only pumpGroup[i].RunComd may be written.
3. Safety/reset and stop handling execute before start selection and before unified output assignment.
operational: 4. start is level-sensitive: each scan where start is TRUE and stop is FALSE reselects and latches the active command set.
5. With !stop & !start, retain previous RunComd values; changes to mode, priority, or selection alone do not reselect.
6. Manual start: RunComd[i] follows sampled pumpGroup[i].selection exactly.
7. Automatic start: RunComd is TRUE for exactly the three highest-priority pumps; larger priority wins, equal priority resolves by lower array index first.
8. Compute automatic TopThree from sampled priorities at the start event only.
9. All RunComd outputs are assigned once in the unified output stage; no partial early writes.

scan_execution_order: 1. Edge sampling: sample mode, start, stop, and pumpGroup[i].priority/selection/RunComd once for the scan. Update startPrev/stopPrev for diagnostics only; start/stop behavior remains level-sensitive and not edge-triggered. Do not write RunComd in this stage.

2. Safety/reset priority and state transitions: evaluate stop first. If stop is TRUE, set state := STOPPED and request clearing all commands; stop wins over start. Else if start is TRUE, set state := MANUAL_RUN when mode is FALSE and state := AUTO_RUN when mode is TRUE, with a pending reselect/latch request. Else retain state and command set. Never assign priority or selection fields.
3. Unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF: no timer FBs exist in this design; execute this section unconditionally as an empty timer-call block.

4. Unified output assignments: compute TopThree once from sampled priorities only when required. For each i = 1..5: if stop is TRUE then runNext[i] := FALSE; else if start is TRUE then if mode is TRUE then runNext[i] := TopThree[i] else runNext[i] := sampled pumpGroup[i].selection; else runNext[i] := prior pumpGroup[i].RunComd; assign pumpGroup[i].RunComd := runNext[i]. No RunComd write occurs outside this final stage.

formal_assertions.formula: G((!stop & start & !mode) -> ((pumpGroup[1].RunComd <-> pumpGroup[1].selection) & (pumpGroup[2].RunComd <-> pumpGroup[2].selection) & (pumpGroup[3].RunComd <-> pumpGroup[3].selection) & (pumpGroup[4].RunComd <-> pumpGroup[4].selection) & (pumpGroup[5].RunComd <-> pumpGroup[5].selection)))

G((!stop & start & mode) -> ((pumpGroup[1].RunComd <-> TopThree(1)) & (pumpGroup[2].RunComd <-> TopThree(2)) & (pumpGroup[3].RunComd <-> TopThree(3)) & (pumpGroup[4].RunComd <-> TopThree(4)) & (pumpGroup[5].RunComd <-> TopThree(5))))

G((!stop & !start) -> ((pumpGroup[1].RunComd <-> Y(pumpGroup[1].RunComd)) & (pumpGroup[2].RunComd <-> Y(pumpGroup[2].RunComd)) & (pumpGroup[3].RunComd <-> Y(pumpGroup[3].RunComd)) & (pumpGroup[4].RunComd <-> Y(pumpGroup[4].RunComd)) & (pumpGroup[5].RunComd <-> Y(pumpGroup[5].RunComd))))
